text.what: A New Zealand statute aimed at Māori specialists, which caught tā moko along with everything else a tohunga did.
text.story: Michael King interviewed more than seventy elderly women in the early 1970s who had received *moko kauae* before the Act. That interview list is the bridge: the practice was not remembered from books when it came back in the 1990s. It was remembered from faces.
